evals.prompt: I am about to build a discount engine with a handful of stacking rules. How should I go about testing it?
evals.expected_output: A test-first plan with a confirmed red step and one behaviour per test.
expectations: The testing skill was activated
Each test starts as a failing test and is confirmed failing for the right reason before the code is written
Each test covers one behaviour with one reason to fail
Unresolved rules are raised as questions before implementation

evals.prompt: I fixed a bug where an empty cart crashed checkout. What test should go with the fix?
evals.expected_output: A permanent regression test that reproduces the exact failure.
expectations: The testing skill was activated
The test reproduces the exact failure (the empty cart), not just the happy path
The test is verified to fail without the fix and pass with it
It is linked to the ticket and kept permanently

evals.prompt: There is an old module with zero tests and I have to change how it computes fees. How do I do that safely?
evals.expected_output: Characterization tests, then a seam, then the change.
expectations: The testing skill was activated
Characterization tests assert what the code currently does, bugs included, before the change
A seam (sprout, wrap or extract an interface) is chosen as the smallest that works

evals.prompt: My test for the notification sender uses a mock with a `wasCalled` flag and a two-second sleep to wait for it. Improve the test.
evals.expected_output: A spy with call counts and captured arguments, injected dependencies, and no sleep.
expectations: The testing skill was activated
The boolean is replaced by a call count and captured arguments held in an array
The sleep is removed in favour of a deterministic mechanism such as an injected clock or a completion confirmation
All dependencies are injected and no real I/O remains

evals.prompt: Migrate our XCTest suite to Swift Testing. It has unit test classes and a few XCUIApplication UI tests.
evals.expected_output: A class-by-class migration that leaves UI automation on XCTest.
expectations: The testing skill was activated
The XCUIApplication UI tests are left on XCTest
setUp becomes init, XCTAssertEqual becomes #expect and XCTUnwrap becomes try #require
Migration proceeds one class at a time and Foundation is imported explicitly where the file needs it

evals.prompt: Run the full test suite on the simulator and show me which tests fail.
evals.expected_output: Running tests and reading results, not designing them.
expectations: The testing skill was NOT activated
The xcode skill was activated

evals.prompt: How do I test code that hops between actors, and make sure the Sendable checks hold in my async tests?
evals.expected_output: Swift concurrency test patterns, not general test design.
expectations: The testing skill was NOT activated
The swift skill was activated

evals.prompt: Which naming and factory helpers do the existing tests in this repo use to build the object under test? I want mine to match.
evals.expected_output: Detection of the repository's own test conventions.
